title: Deployment & Production
blurb: The unglamorous part: APIs, latency budgets, caching, rate limits, secrets, multi-tenancy, cost engineering, the LLMOps stack. This is where AI engineers earn their keep.

nodes.label: API design for LLM products
nodes.description: Streaming vs batch endpoints, idempotency, request schemas, error semantics, versioning. The user-facing contract that has to absorb LLM weirdness.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a streaming LLM endpoint contract and defend the error-semantics choices.

nodes.label: Latency budgets & SLOs
nodes.description: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, end-to-end budgets, time-to-first-token vs time-to-last-token, SLO/SLA distinctions, error budgets.
nodes.doneWhen: You can set realistic latency SLOs for an LLM feature and decompose them by stage.

nodes.label: Caching strategies (prompt cache, semantic cache)
nodes.description: Provider-native prompt caching (Anthropic, OpenAI), semantic caching at the application layer, cache invalidation, the safety question of caching personalized output.
nodes.doneWhen: You can pick between prompt caching and semantic caching for a feature and quantify the hit rate.

nodes.label: Rate limiting & fallback
nodes.description: Token-bucket and concurrency limits, model-failover (primary → secondary), graceful degradation, queueing under load.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a fallback policy that survives a primary-model outage without users noticing.

nodes.label: Secrets, keys & access control
nodes.description: API key handling, per-tenant keys, BYOK, signing, the on-call horror story of leaked credentials in logs.
nodes.doneWhen: You can audit an LLM service for credential handling and find at least one weakness.

nodes.label: Multi-tenant patterns
nodes.description: Per-tenant rate limits, per-tenant model routing, per-tenant evals and cost, isolation. The B2B reality of every AI product company.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe how a multi-tenant LLM platform isolates noisy-neighbor workloads.

nodes.label: MLOps / LLMOps
nodes.description: Model registries, prompt registries, dataset versioning, eval-as-CI, blue/green model swaps, the standard ops loop for an LLM product team.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe a basic LLMOps pipeline and identify the difference from classical MLOps.

nodes.label: Cost engineering at scale
nodes.description: Model routing, distillation in production, batch jobs, off-peak inference, the tradeoff curve between cost and quality at scale.
nodes.doneWhen: You can take a $10k/month LLM bill and design a plan to cut it 50% without losing user-visible quality.
